reviewerOrPass: Worker B, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: After the record was frozen, the same AI reconstructed the 180 EC from the 2026–2027 regulations and the programme table. It checked the field school and thesis entry requirements from the individual courses and reconsidered the workable third-year elective placement. The workbook was rescanned for archaeology, GIS, sampling and material analysis. It tested the strongest integrated candidate on actual course contributions before checking the final exception and wording.
findings: The 2026–2027 regulations for ACASA Archaeology are adopted by both faculties. Articles 11.1, 11.3 and 11.4 and appendix 4 establish the common 180 EC, with 60 first-year EC, 60 second-year EC, and a third year of 18 required taught EC, 30 electives and a 12 EC thesis including colloquium. The English track and its thesis are selected without stacking Dutch equivalents. Philosophy of the Humanities is second year and Lieux de mémoire third. VU’s dated admissions explanation clarifies that formal joint awarding starts in 2027–2028. The 2026–2027 UvA target remains the reviewed identity. The programme has a language diagnostic, an ACASA orientation and recurring tutoring outside the credit total. The English OER is the institutional translation and the curriculum claims were cross-checked against current UvA and VU guides.

Complete the first 60 EC, exceeding the 48 EC study-advice threshold. Year 1 moves from interpreting sources and past environments to excavation and recording in Field School 1. Year 2 adds science, theory, digital analysis, materials and heritage, followed by Field School 2 after Field School 1. The UvA catalogue identifies Field School 2 as 110221216Y, while the joint regulations list 110226116Y alongside VU code L_AABAARC212. The regulations list Field School 1 under 110121046Y, while the retained record reference ends 110121146Y. The excursion similarly has the retained reference 138221066Y while the regulations list 138221026Y beside L_AABAAGO204. Title, year, purpose and six credits identify each as a single curricular unit. Appendix 4 places From Excavation to Publication and Lieux de mémoire in autumn and Death and Commemoration in spring. The 30 EC free elective space can be spread across the year, so it is not forced into a full autumn alongside the 12 compulsory autumn credits. Complete all first- and second-year required courses before the thesis. A standard minor or eligible electives may fill the open space. Outside choices require permission where specified; internship use is capped at 12 EC. The overlapping Archaeology Today minor is excluded under article 12.2.

The strongest integrated response combines three substantive archaeology/material-culture courses with heritage, spatial analysis and Earth-science practicals. World Archaeology provides object description and technical drawing, Greek Archaeology uses material evidence to understand ancient political life, and Heritage and Ancient Democracy combines primary texts and archaeological material with civic interpretation. African Art and Heritage and Modern Art and Modern Museums add research on collections, interpretation and public exhibition. Description-only Greek Archaeology, Renaissance Italy and Global Mediterranean, and Writing Art’s Histories have real contributions in material evidence, art exchange and interpretive method. Earth Observation and description-only Spatial Planning teach GIS and remote sensing. Dynamic Earth provides geological stratigraphy and field measurement. Soils and Aquifers adds field sampling and environmental laboratories. Digital imaging and data science also contribute transferable methods. The combined palette lacks repeated excavation and recording of human deposits, finds processing, disciplinary materials analysis and the research-to-publication progression. Filling out 24 courses would materially shift the centre to heritage, general humanities or environmental science. None of the three candidates sustains sufficient archaeology as a whole programme. This judgment follows course content independently of terms and availability.
